correctness.rationale: Rank-one Dirichlet resolvent produces the exact sign equation. Explicit cosine inequalities cover 0<r≤1; the logarithmic hyperbolic comparison covers 1<r≤101 and 101<r≤1+9/δ²; a strict derivative lower bound covers all larger r. Thus one positive crossing exists. At this crossing a bounded exponential remainder and inversion of y−log y prove the leading log and loglog terms. Finite independent Python bisections verify examples without substituting for the analytic all-δ proof.

value.rationale: A reset destination approaching an absorbing boundary is an intrinsic ecological boundary regime. The quantitative minimum reset intensity becomes extraordinarily large. The theorem turns a numerical qualitative phase diagram into a rigorous global crossover and an explicit two-term rate law, identifying how close-to-edge relocation must accelerate to rescue linear growth. This is directly useful for interpreting the existing model without an invented downstream theorem.
